summary.headline: Fineotex H1 FY27 consolidated total income rose 166.8% YoY to INR778.13 crore and PAT rose 81.5% to INR92.75 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported H1 FY27 consolidated total income of INR778.13 crore (up 166.8% YoY), operating EBITDA of INR118.74 crore (up 111.2%) and PAT of INR92.75 crore (up 81.5%), with business volumes up about 132.3%. Q2 alone showed total income of about INR391 crore (up 169%), operating EBITDA of about INR60 crore (up 92%) and PAT of about INR45 crore (up 71%). Growth is largely driven by the CrudeChem Technologies Group (53.33% stake, acquired December 2025) and the oil and gas vertical, while the Q1 to Q2 sequential revenue from CrudeChem appeared flat to slightly lower, which management attributed to timing of orders. Management also flagged lower other income in Q2 and higher COGS, and guided to a structurally lower tax rate of 17-20%.

segments.name: Oil and gas specialty chemicals (incl. CrudeChem, US; India export)
segments.commentary: Management put the oil and gas share of revenue at about 65%. CrudeChem's annual business was about $50 million before acquisition and is now annualised at about $100 million; a $200 million revenue target is stated for calendar 2028.

segments.name: Textile specialty chemicals
segments.commentary: Share has fallen to about 25% of revenue from about 90% in 2022, though absolute revenue has grown. Management says textile demand is recovering on lower US tariffs and new India, UK and EU trade arrangements.

segments.name: Cleaning and hygiene
segments.commentary: Contributes about 7-8% of revenue; management expects this segment to pick up on sustainability and cost-reduction demand.

segments.name: Water and wastewater treatment (Fineotex America Inc.)
segments.commentary: New, early-stage vertical targeting data centres and semiconductors. Management expects order inflows by Q4 FY27 and says no revenue contribution has been quantified yet.

guidance_outlook: Management targets INR3,000 crore revenue by FY28; current run rate is about INR1,600 crore (last two quarters annualised), and management said FY29 is also possible if the target is missed.
CrudeChem revenue target of about $200 million is for calendar 2028; management said it should be achievable in the next 6-7 quarters.
Effective tax rate expected at 17-20% going forward, with 20% cited as a good planning figure, given Section 115BAB (15%) for the new Indian plant subsidiary and lower US rates.
Management expects to raise CrudeChem stake from about 54% to about 79-80% when promoters sell 25% in January 2028 under the SPAs.
Management expects to be at least 3x, possibly 4x, current scale in 6-7 years; no 2030 numeric target was given.
Management expects the AquaStrike Premium product certification to start generating orders in the current financial year.
capex_capacity: CrudeChem US manufacturing platform at Brookshire and Midland, Texas has about 148,000 metric tons of stated annual capacity.

No quantified capex plan for the next 2-3 years was given; management said the water business asset turnover should be at least 5x-6x and that funding can come from internal accruals, cash on books, debt or equity.
CrudeChem has added product lines and technology transfers from India to the US to avoid freight and lead-time issues from Asia and the Middle East.
Plant for the Indian operations was commissioned about 2 years ago under FSPL Specialties, a wholly owned subsidiary.
Two new wholly owned subsidiaries, Fineotex Holdings Inc. and Fineotex America Inc., were incorporated in the last two months; future acquisitions are to be routed through them at 100% ownership.
demand_pricing: Management says oil and gas customers are moving to spot purchases and short 1-2 month contracts; Aramco has reportedly cancelled its old long-term contracts and a war surcharge concept has emerged.

Management cited a rise in US rig count and said CrudeChem demand can be lumpy quarter to quarter because orders slip between periods; it said Q2 CrudeChem revenue was flat-to-slightly-lower sequentially and reiterated it is not a decline.
Management said Middle East oil and gas customers are increasingly buying from India at ADIPEC; Aramco is a customer, and Canada and Guyana/Suriname are new supply areas.

Management attributed higher COGS (up about 6% per the analyst) to inventory timing, freight disruption and longer Asia-US transit; said prices are usually passed through in 1-2 months and competition was not the issue.
Other expenses were said to have dropped about 6% as new-product spend in CrudeChem normalised; other income fell in Q2 on lower treasury and dividend income and forex effects.
Management said CrudeChem has 44% sustainable products and claimed 17-18% customer cost savings in fracking and completion applications.

qa_highlights.question: Can PAT margins return to 16% (FY26) or the 21% FY24 peak?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said operational efficiencies from acquisitions take time; CrudeChem EBITDA margin moved from single digit to double digit by Q4 FY26, and blended margins should move closer to historic levels in the next couple of years, without giving a number.

qa_highlights.question: Why did CrudeChem sequential revenue appear flat or down in Q2 versus Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is lumpy and should be judged annually; orders slip between quarters, and CrudeChem annualised revenue has gone from about $50 million to about $100 million since acquisition.

qa_highlights.question: Will equity be diluted to fund acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is 'not a no, no, but not a yes, yes'; acquisitions will be EBITDA accretive, funding will be routed via the new 100%-owned subsidiaries, and debt is possible as a bridge.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a capex figure for the water treatment business?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no figure; said internal accruals and cash on books are substantial and an asset turnover of at least 5x-6x is targeted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR3,000 crore FY28 revenue target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the current run rate is about INR1,600 crore; the target may slip to FY29 but the company expects to be well ahead of plan, with margin recovery toward the historic 20% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of AquaStrike Premium certification in India?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant was audited by CIB, the product is registered, and orders are expected to start in the current financial year.

risks_watch: CrudeChem quarterly revenue lumpiness and dependence on rig counts, geopolitics, freight costs and weather; management wants annual, not quarterly, assessment.
Margin dilution from COGS inflation and inventory destocking; PAT margin has moderated from the FY24 peak (about 21%) to about 16% in FY26.
Other income decline and the reliance of PAT on tax benefits; management guided that the 17-20% effective tax rate will rise above the Q2 level of about 21-22%.
Equity dilution risk and funding plan for acquisitions and the water business, with no quantified capex or revenue for Fineotex America.
Textile segment has fallen to about 25% of revenue, so mix shift to oil and gas increases concentration.
Management did not give a 2030 revenue target; its 3x-4x outlook is qualitative and conditional on assumed stable geopolitics.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on the outlook for oil and gas and water, with repeated caveats that trends are unpredictable. Evasive on specifics: capex, water revenue timing, FY28 revenue path and the equity dilution question were answered qualitatively, and the response to the CrudeChem sequential revenue question was defensive.
key_quotes: Consolidated total income grew by 166.8% year-on-year to INR778.13 crores.
We have been able to bring the single-digit EBITDA margin company into double digits.
So we always endeavor to do that.
I think we should be at least 3x from where we are and/or maybe 4x minimum.

adds.what: CrudeChem US manufacturing platform at Brookshire and Midland, Texas, about 148,000 metric tons stated annual capacity (existing, not a new addition)

growth.why: Management targets INR3,000 cr revenue by FY28 (run rate ~INR1,600 cr) but later said it may slip to FY29, and CrudeChem's US$200m target is for CY2028 described as only 'broadly' achievable; backing is mostly aspiration with no quarterly path, no new capacity and no quantified capex, while Q2 revenue grew 169% YoY on acquisition effects.

oneOffs.what: CrudeChem Technologies Group (53.33% stake, acquired December 2025) consolidated into Q2 FY27 totals; drives the bulk of the ~169% Q2 total income growth
Brief does not say the year-ago quarter was weak or disrupted, so no low-base adjustment is recorded

quality.why: Q2 FY27 total income rose about 169% to roughly INR391 crore, but the brief attributes the growth largely to the CrudeChem acquisition consolidated from December 2025, which is inorganic and will lap after about a year; CrudeChem revenue was flat-to-slightly-lower sequentially in Q2, and business volumes rose about 132.3% over H1 with no organic split given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management said blended margins should move closer to historic levels over the next couple of years without a number; PAT margin is about 16% in FY26 versus the 21% FY24 peak, and CrudeChem EBITDA margin moved from single digit to double digit by Q4 FY26, but Q2 COGS rose about 6% and other income fell.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new capacity was announced; the 148,000 MT Texas capacity is existing, and no quantified capex plan for the next 2-3 years was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 business volumes are up about 132.3% YoY and CrudeChem annualised revenue has gone from about $50m to about $100m, though management said quarterly orders are lumpy (Q2 CrudeChem revenue flat to slightly lower sequentially).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex figure was given for the water business or the next 2-3 years, but management says funding is available from internal accruals and cash on books and targets asset turnover of 5x-6x, so an acquisition or capex announcement is plausible without a stated date.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is not raising guidance: the INR3,000 crore FY28 target is unconfirmed (run rate about INR1,600 crore) and may slip to FY29, and the US$200m CrudeChem target is only 'broadly' achievable by CY2028.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management already said the INR3,000 crore FY28 target may slip to FY29, and CrudeChem revenue is lumpy with Q2 flat to slightly lower sequentially, while COGS and freight pressures persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AquaStrike Premium is registered and management expects it to start generating orders in the current FY; water and wastewater order inflows are expected by Q4 FY27 with no revenue quantified.

rows.label: Water treatment order inflows (Fineotex America)
rows.why: Management expects order inflows by Q4 FY27 for the data centre and semiconductor vertical, but no revenue contribution has been quantified.

rows.label: CrudeChem stake rise to 79-80%
rows.why: Promoters are contracted under the SPAs to sell 25% in January 2028, taking the stake from about 54% to about 79-80%.

rows.label: Middle East and new supply areas (Aramco, Canada, Guyana/Suriname)
rows.why: Middle East customers are buying more from India and Aramco is a customer, but no volume or revenue number was given for these new areas.

tone.note: Management was confident on oil and gas demand, the CrudeChem stake step-up and the AquaStrike launch, but cautious and evasive on capex, water revenue timing, the FY28 INR3,000 crore path and equity dilution; analysts pushed on the flat CrudeChem sequential revenue and margin recovery.
